newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EMU stability pact seen delayed until 97.
newsitem.headline: EMU stability pact seen delayed until 97.

text.p: German insistance on a tough post-EMU budget stability pact means a final decision on the accord is not now expected until next year, European Union officials said on Monday.

"It's not going to be done by December," said one official familiar with the deliberations of the EU's monetary committee. Officials had hoped to agree a pact at the December 13-14 summit of EU leaders in Dublin.

In spite of rising optimism over the pace of negotiations on a pact that would fine countries running budget deficits above three percent of total output, EU monetary officials say Germany is set to reiterate its demands for much tougher accord.

The EU's monetary committee is due to gather for a regularly scheduled meeting on Tuesday and Wednesday and will discuss the budget pact along with other issues related to economic and monetary union.
"It is very well possible that in Dublin there will be a political declaration of the stability pact and the legal text will be adopted next year," said another senior EU official.
One of Germany's primary objectives is to quantify the precise economic conditions under which a country running an excessive deficit would avoid sanctions.
